audit.whatIsWrong: Warrior Trickster is the pivot of the whole entry — 'wait for his decoy', 'hold your big cooldowns until you've seen the clone resolve' — and its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: It is 22 seconds at rank 1. That number is the entire instruction: waiting out a clone is a plan when the punish window is twenty-two seconds long, and it is not a plan if you think the ability is up again shortly. The invisibility half also matters and is only mentioned in passing — he goes invisible AND dashes as the clone spawns, and Ambessa carries no reveal, so the tell is the dash direction rather than the clone itself.
audit.corrected: Warrior Trickster (W), 22/21/20/19/18: he turns invisible, dashes, and leaves a clone behind. Refuse the bait and he has no engage for 22 seconds.
sources: champ-data/_kits/wukong.json — W Warrior Trickster 'becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone', cd 22/21/20/19/18

audit.whatIsWrong: Nimbus Strike is called a 'gap-closer' and 'engage dash' throughout, with no mention that it is TARGETED and no cooldown given.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike dashes to a targeted enemy — which includes minions — so 'stand out of his dash range' is not the counterplay a player would infer from the current text. He reaches you through the wave whenever a minion is between you, which reframes both the safe-farming advice and the disengage plan: you cannot outspace it, you can only punish the 10-second window after he spends it. Its cooldown is 10s at rank 1 and 7s at rank 5.
audit.corrected: Nimbus Strike (E), 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7, 650 range: a TARGETED dash — a minion between you is a gap-close. Punish the 10s after he spends it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/wukong.json — E Nimbus Strike 'dashes to a targeted enemy', cd 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7, range 650

audit.why: The entry's central claim — that Public Execution locks the real Wukong rather than the decoy — checks out against Riot's text, which says she blinks to the farthest enemy CHAMPION in the chosen line. A clone is not a champion, so it cannot be selected. This is the one Ambessa-side claim in my slice that survived verification intact, and it is the reason level 6 is her window; I sharpened the wording to say WHY rather than deleting or hedging it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — R Public Execution: 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing'

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[1].why: 'Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade.' Ambessa's passive grants no shield. Crushing Blow is also never given a cooldown despite being the reason her damage falls off in a long trade.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step gives a dash, an empowered next attack and an energy refund; Repudiation (W) is the shield, and it braces before it slams with damage blocked during the brace amplifying the slam. Crushing Blow is an 8-second auto-reset that gains attack range and cuts armour, so it is both the best thing to brace and the reason an extended trade drifts to Wukong — a number the entry needs and does not have.
audit.corrected: Repudiation (W) is the shield — brace Crushing Blow. Crushing Blow (Q), 8/7.5/7/6.5/6: bonus range, bonus damage, armour cut, and it resets his attack.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — P Drakehound's Step, W Repudiation
champ-data/_kits/wukong.json — Q Crushing Blow cd 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, autoReset

audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 with Wukong carry threat 7/10 matches both the data (50.34% over 584 games — the closest to a true coinflip in the slice) and the kit: two melee bruisers with dashes, one armour-stacking passive against all-physical damage, one clone bait against a blink that ignores clones. Unchanged.
sources: packet ambessa.json — wukong winRate 50.34 over 584 games

notes: This is the healthiest Ambessa entry in my slice — no invented 'R armor-pen / on-ability healing' text, no reversed mechanic, and a level chart that agrees with its own prose. The only generic defect present is the shared phases[1].why boilerplate claiming her passive shields, which I fixed. STILL WORTH KNOWING: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json tags Public Execution (R) with 'heal' and tags W and R with 'grounding', none of which Riot's descriptions support (the parser caught 'slams the ground'); this entry simply never leaned on the bad flag. Stone Skin grants max health REGENERATION as well as stacking armour, which is what the existing 'Anti-heal early — his healing fights your pattern' itemization line is presumably built on; I left that line intact since the regen makes it defensible. WIN RATE: MC_WR_TABLES.ambessa.wukong and the packet agree exactly at 50.34 over 584 games.
